draft: Chapter 8 - The Road Owed to the Dead (Draft 3, combined).md
chapter: ../Chapter 8 - The Road Owed to the Dead.md
intro_md: 1 October 2026. The author's combined version of Chapter 8 (`Drafts/Chapter 8 - The Road Owed to the Dead (Draft 3, combined).md`, from their Word file, with straight quotes) is now the chapter. Only the house style is changed here. Claude's notes on it are in `Chapter 8 - Design.md` ("The combined version"), waiting on the author. The version after Claude's three passes is saved as Draft 2, and its changes stay in `Chapter 8 - Changes.md`.

sections.Notes: Claude's notes on the combined version, agreed (1 October)
sections.Pass 1: Pass 1: errors, POV slips and logic
sections.Review notes: The review notes: compression and small fixes
sections.100/100: Claude's 100/100 review: the guards, Marta, the auctioned woman and "looked"

changes.title: The heading
changes.before: **Chapter 8 – The Road Owed to the Dead**
changes.after: # Chapter 8 – The Road Owed to the Dead
changes.why: The chapters' heading format.
changes.decision_note: House style only; the author's text is otherwise unchanged.

changes.title: Faint (1)
changes.before: "Because she's 『Faint』. Only 『Faint』 can be sold, and those guards know it as well as he does."
changes.after: "Because she's Faint. Only Faint can be sold, and those guards know it as well as he does."
changes.why: Chapter 1 writes "Faint" without the corner brackets, which the house style keeps for 『Affinity』 and 『Magic』.
changes.decision_note: Rejected (1 October): the author wants 『Faint』 with corner brackets wherever it's used ("apply 『Faint』 to all chapter where it is used").

changes.title: Faint (2)
changes.before: *Only 『Faint』 can be sold.* Gerolt hadn't known what they would do with someone who had none. Alaric pulled the cloak closer round himself. He didn't want to imagine what else they could do.
changes.after: *Only Faint can be sold.* Gerolt hadn't known what they would do with someone who had none. Alaric pulled the cloak closer round himself. He didn't want to imagine what else they could do.
changes.why: As above.
changes.decision_note: Rejected (1 October): the author wants 『Faint』 with corner brackets wherever it's used ("apply 『Faint』 to all chapter where it is used").

changes.title: The south gate
changes.before: "The farmer's niece. Just inside the South Gate. They want her questioned after she closes."
changes.after: "The farmer's niece. They want her questioned after she closes."
changes.why: Lower case, as in Chapters 2 and 6 (pass 3 of 1 October). 100/100 review: Both guards know where Marta's inn is; the address was for the reader.
changes.decision_note: House style only; the author's text is otherwise unchanged.

changes.title: Silas, not "the man"
changes.before: Alaric looked at Silas. The man was watching the guards through the space between two barrels.
changes.after: Silas was watching the guards through the space between two barrels.
changes.why: The narration had already named Silas, and the author asked for less "the man". 100/100 review: Fewer looks.
changes.decision_note: Note 1: "Use Silas" (1 October).

changes.title: In the shadow of a doorway
changes.before: Silas stopped beneath the eaves and held out his good hand.
changes.after: Silas stopped in the shadow of a doorway and held out his good hand.
changes.why: "Eaves" is one of the words the author didn't know.
changes.decision_note: Note 2: "Use in the shadow" (1 October).

changes.title: Which voices
changes.before: The voices round the table grew quieter. Later came the sound of dishes being washed, then a window shutting. One by one, the lights along the backs of the houses went out. Silas went to look through the door again and returned without beckoning him over.
changes.after: The voices in the houses grew quieter. Later came the sound of dishes being washed, then a window shutting. One by one, the lights along the row went out.
changes.why: The family's table was several houses back, so "the table" was unclear. Final pass: "The houses" was twice in a row ("The voices in the houses grew quieter"). Review notes: Silas checks the door three times during the wait. The middle check goes.
changes.decision_note: Note 3: agreed (1 October).

changes.title: The other cart
changes.before: Silas moved with her along the side of the loaded cart. For a moment its sacks hid them from the patrol. Then Wena tried to get round its rear wheel and whined, high enough that Alaric heard her over the voices in the street.
changes.after: Silas moved with her along the side of the other cart. Its sacks hid them from the patrol. Then Wena tried to get round its rear wheel and whined, high enough that Alaric heard her over the voices in the street.
changes.why: Three carts were in play. Silas walks beside the one being backed in, and Alaric hides behind the half-unloaded one. *Pass 2:* Cuts one of three "for a moment"s in the chapter.
changes.decision_note: Note 4: agreed (1 October).

changes.title: The half-unloaded cart
changes.before: Alaric stepped behind the cart. He kept close to its load, with the hood pulled forward and the bundle against his chest. Wena's whine went on a moment longer, then stopped.
changes.after: Alaric stepped behind the half-unloaded cart. He kept close to its load, with the hood pulled forward and the bundle against his chest. Wena's whine went on a moment longer, then stopped.
changes.why: As above: it's clear which cart he hides behind.
changes.decision_note: Note 4: agreed (1 October).

changes.title: Tying the bed
changes.before: Alaric rested the sword across his knees while Silas rolled the bed again, keeping his burned hand clear of the knot. Alaric tied the cord round it. Silas tucked it beneath his arm and took Wena's lead with his good hand.
changes.after: He rested the sword across his knees while Silas rolled the bed again, keeping his burned hand clear. Alaric tied the cord round it for him. Silas tucked it beneath his arm and took Wena's lead with his good hand.
changes.why: Two paragraphs in a row began with "Alaric", and the knot was split across two sentences. Review notes: The old sentence could make Silas the one tying the cord.
changes.decision_note: Note 5: agreed (1 October).

changes.title: Thanks, lad
changes.before: "Cheers, lad."
changes.after: "Thanks, lad."
changes.why: "Cheers" was the only very modern British phrase in the chapters.
changes.decision_note: Note 6: agreed (1 October).

changes.title: Hands on the way down
changes.before: There was no moon yet. They went down the slope with only the lights of the town to walk towards, Silas first, then Alaric with the bundle under one arm and Wena close against his legs. At the bottom, a cart track ran along the edge of the fields towards the wall. The carts had cut it into ruts and the ruts had dried hard, and after the first dozen steps every one of them seemed to be exactly where Alaric put his foot.
changes.after: There was no moon yet. They went down the slope with only the lights of the town to walk towards, Silas first, then Alaric with the bundle under one arm and Wena's lead in his other hand. At the bottom, a cart track ran along the edge of the fields towards the wall. The carts had cut it into ruts and the ruts had dried hard, and after the first dozen steps every one of them seemed to be exactly where Alaric put his foot.
changes.why: Silas had just given him the lead; the sentence didn't say where it was.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Who keeps the lead short
changes.before: Wena's nose went up towards the window. He kept the lead short and followed Silas past it.
changes.after: Wena's nose went up towards the window. Alaric kept the lead short and followed Silas past it.
changes.why: "He" came straight after a sentence about Wena.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: The door in the wall
changes.before: At the end of the row, Silas turned into a gap between a house and a lean-to. Beyond it, the passage ended at the wall. Bundles of kindling stood along one side; a broken handcart had been pushed against the other. Set into the stone behind it was a narrow timber door.
changes.after: At the end of the row, Silas turned into a gap between a house and a lean-to. Beyond the lean-to, the gap narrowed into a passage that ended at the wall. Bundles of kindling stood along one side; a broken handcart had been pushed against the other. In the wall at the end was a narrow timber door.
changes.why: "The passage" hadn't been introduced, and "behind it" could mean behind the handcart.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: The handcart
changes.before: Silas pointed Alaric towards the broken cart. They crouched behind it, and Wena settled under the axle against Alaric's calf.
changes.after: Silas pointed Alaric towards the broken handcart. They crouched behind it, and Wena settled under the axle against Alaric's calf.
changes.why: The same handcart as the paragraph before, not one of the yard's carts.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Who whispers
changes.before: "That door?" he whispered.
changes.after: "That door?" Alaric whispered.
changes.why: After a sentence ending on "Alaric's calf", "he" could have been Silas.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Wetting the binding
changes.before: Silas loosened the binding on his palm. Alaric held the water skin while he wet it a little at a time. When they had finished, Silas put the skin back in the sack and rested his hand on his knee.
changes.after: Silas loosened the binding on his palm. Alaric held the water skin and poured, a little at a time, while Silas wet the cloth. When they had finished, Silas put the skin back in the sack and rested his hand on his knee.
changes.why: "He" could have been either of them.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Silas's arm
changes.before: Their boots scraped away across the yard. Silas kept his forearm against Alaric's arm until the voices had gone.
changes.after: Their boots went back out through the cart entrance. Silas's hand was on Alaric's sleeve, and it stayed there until the voices had gone.
changes.why: "Kept" implied the arm had been put there earlier, and it hadn't. Review notes: The forearm is kept for the tub. Error pass: The guards came in through the cart entrance, and the loader "went out after the guards" while watching it. "Across the yard" sent them the wrong way.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Which stall
changes.before: Instead, he stopped beside the stall. The man with the baskets had put one down and was asking about the cloth. Alaric turned towards it too, leaving the man between himself and Wena. If he kept walking, she would keep pulling.
changes.after: Instead, he stopped beside the nearest stall. The man with the baskets had put one down and was asking the woman about her cloth. Alaric turned towards it too, leaving the man between himself and Wena. If he kept walking, she would keep pulling.
changes.why: "The stall" hadn't been picked out yet. Error pass: "The cloth" was also Wena's lead in the same scene ("Silas shortened the cloth"). This is the woman with cloth over her arm.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Who finds Silas
changes.before: He found Silas a few paces away, holding Wena close.
changes.after: Alaric found Silas a few paces away, holding Wena close.
changes.why: After a sentence about the woman, "He" was unclear. This is also the approved dialogue's wording.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Which woman
changes.before: Alaric shut his eyes. He saw the chain tighten before the woman had got both feet off the boards.
changes.after: Alaric shut his eyes. He saw the chain again, pulling tight before the woman from the platform had both feet down.
changes.why: "The woman" came straight after the woman with the tub, so she's now "the woman from the platform". The line echoes the auction ("before she had both feet on the ground") without repeating it word for word.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: Who stood by the door
changes.before:
Then she was in the shed, putting the trays down and calling to someone further inside. Silas brought Alaric out before she could turn back.

For a moment he stood beside the door with his hand still raised. She hadn't asked him anything else.

"This way," Silas said.
changes.after:
Then she was in the shed, putting the trays down and calling to someone further inside. Alaric stood by the door with his hand still raised. She hadn't asked him anything else.

Silas drew him away before she could turn back. "This way."
changes.why: Silas brought Alaric away from the door, and then "he" stood beside it, so the order was backwards and "he" could have meant Silas. Alaric now stands there first and Silas draws him away. It also drops one of the chapter's "for a moment"s. "This way" joins Silas's paragraph, so his name isn't said twice in a row.
changes.decision_note: Pass 1 of three (1 October): errors, POV slips and logic.

changes.title: The walkway
changes.before: It opened into a covered strip along the side of the building. A woman carrying a stack of wooden trays was coming towards them. Silas stepped back, and Alaric moved out of her way.
changes.after: It opened into a covered walkway along the side of the building. A woman carrying a stack of wooden trays was coming towards them. Silas stepped back, and Alaric moved out of her way.
changes.why: "Covered strip" is an odd phrase for something plain.
changes.decision_note: Pass 2 of three (1 October): vocabulary, rhythm and repeats.

changes.title: The guard's search
changes.before: The guard looked into the crowd, slowly, one face after another. His eyes went across the sacks. Alaric stayed still, with his boot braced against the wheel so that his ankle wouldn't give.
changes.after: The guard turned to the crowd and went over it slowly, one face after another. His eyes passed across the sacks. Alaric stayed still, with his boot braced against the wheel so that his ankle wouldn't give.
changes.why: Three "looked"s in three paragraphs.
changes.decision_note: Pass 2 of three (1 October): vocabulary, rhythm and repeats.

changes.title: Where they wait
changes.before: Silas didn't slow down. He took them past the front and round the corner, into a lane that ran along the side of the inn to its back door. Across from it was a recess between a closed storehouse and its boundary wall. From there, they could see the private entrance beyond a stack of empty barrels and the light from a window beside it. Through the mouth of the lane, Alaric could see customers leaving the front step.
changes.after: Silas didn't slow down. He took them past the front and round the corner, into a lane that ran along the side of the inn to its back door. Across from it was a narrow space between a closed storehouse and its yard wall. From there, they could see the back door beyond a stack of empty barrels and the light from a window beside it. Through the mouth of the lane, Alaric could see customers leaving the front step.
changes.why: Plainer words than "recess" and "boundary wall". *Pass 3:* Alaric calls it the back door everywhere else, and so do the chapters.
changes.decision_note: Pass 2 of three (1 October): vocabulary, rhythm and repeats.

changes.title: Inwards
changes.before:
At last, the noise in the yard moved away from the wall. The wheels and voices were coming from one place now, further in. Silas went to look, then eased the loose end of the split board aside and reached through with his good hand. A wooden bar scraped out of its bracket. He lowered it inside and pushed the door inward a finger's width.

He listened before beckoning Alaric over.
changes.after: At last, the noise in the yard moved away from the wall. The wheels and voices were coming from one place now, further in. Silas went to the door again, eased the loose end of the split board aside and reached through with his good hand. A wooden bar scraped out of its bracket. He lowered it inside, pushed the door inwards a finger's width and listened before beckoning Alaric over.
changes.why: British house style, as everywhere else in the chapters. Review notes: "He listened before beckoning Alaric over." joins the paragraph before it, one step fewer in the crossing. 100/100 review: Fewer looks.
changes.decision_note: Pass 3 of three, the final pass (1 October): consistency with the earlier chapters and house style.

changes.title: The windows go out
changes.before: The ground-floor windows went dark. Only one stayed lit, at the back beside the door. Something scraped across the floor inside, chairs maybe, and a woman's voice said something short to somebody.
changes.after: The ground-floor windows went out, all but one at the back beside the door. Something scraped across the floor inside, chairs maybe, and a woman's voice said something short to somebody.
changes.why: The author asked for fewer "dark"s. The chapter has "the windows… went out" elsewhere, and Chapter 6 does too. Error pass: "Went out" and then "only one stayed lit" contradicted each other.
changes.decision_note: Pass 3 of three, the final pass (1 October): consistency with the earlier chapters and house style.

changes.title: The fading hum
changes.before: He could feel the hum in the ground for a long time after the ship had passed. It grew fainter and fainter, until he couldn't tell whether it was still there or whether his chest was only remembering it. Down in Kelmend the bell was still ringing, and the torches on the wall were moving towards the gate. The carts on the road had stopped.
changes.after: He could feel the hum in the ground for a long time after the ship had passed. It faded little by little, until he couldn't tell whether it was still there or whether his chest was only remembering it. Down in Kelmend the bell was still ringing, and the torches on the wall were moving towards the gate. The carts on the road had stopped.
changes.why: "Fainter" sits badly in a chapter where "Faint" means people who can be sold, especially in its first paragraph.
changes.decision_note: Final pass (1 October): everything, once more.

changes.title: Round the light
changes.before: It was a single blue-green spark, far out over the trees where the ship had gone, and at first Alaric thought the ship was turning. It wasn't. The ship's light went on shrinking towards the river, and this one grew. A narrow hull took shape around it. It came back over the wood, low enough that Wena flattened herself against him, and on across the fields with a thin, high hum of its own. It passed over the end of the wall by the gate. Then it sank behind the roofs and didn't come up again.
changes.after: It was a single blue-green spark, far out over the trees where the ship had gone, and at first Alaric thought the ship was turning. It wasn't. The ship's light went on shrinking towards the river, and this one grew. A narrow hull took shape round it. It came back over the wood, low enough that Wena flattened herself against him, and on across the fields with a thin, high hum of its own. It passed over the end of the wall by the gate. Then it sank behind the roofs and didn't come up again.
changes.why: House style: "round", not "around".
changes.decision_note: Final pass (1 October): everything, once more.

changes.title: Who stands at the corner
changes.before: Alaric watched him walk to the corner. He stood there a while, looking both ways, then came back.
changes.after: Alaric watched him walk to the corner. Silas stood there a while, looking both ways, then came back.
changes.why: "He" came straight after "Alaric", so it could have been Alaric standing at the corner.
changes.decision_note: Final pass (1 October): everything, once more.

changes.title: The scraping again
changes.before: Silas kept looking at the door. Alaric waited for him to turn round and answer. Inside, something scraped across the floor; Silas glanced at the handle instead.
changes.after: Silas kept looking at the door. Alaric waited for him to turn round and answer. Inside, the scraping started again; Silas glanced at the handle instead.
changes.why: "Something scraped across the floor inside" was already said when the windows went out. Now it's the same sound coming back, and "the scraping stopped" when Alaric knocks finishes it.
changes.decision_note: Final pass (1 October): everything, once more.

changes.title: The field, told once
changes.before: "I woke up under a dead man! There were bodies all round me, and when I got out from under him there were more, everywhere I looked. Hundreds. Maybe thousands. I couldn't count them."
changes.after: "I've told you! I woke up in a field full of bodies, and I don't remember anything before it."
changes.why: Chapter 3 already has "I woke up on his farm today, under a dead man. There were thousands of them." Only the beastfolk in armour, the machines and "He hadn't heard a battle either" are new. Without "thousands" here, Silas's "I heard 'thousands'" calls back to Chapter 3, where he heard it.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: The field, told once (2)
changes.before: "Men, elves… things with horns and claws. Beastfolk, Gerolt called them, but these were wearing armour. There were silver machines among them, too. One was lying on its side. I don't remember anything before waking up there. I've told you that."
changes.after: "Men, elves… things with horns and claws. Beastfolk, Gerolt called them, but these were wearing armour. There were silver machines among them, too. One was lying on its side."
changes.why: "I've told you" moves to the start of his outburst.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: Silas looks away
changes.before: "With half of Kelmend in there? Some bastard would fetch a guard for the price of his next drink. We'll wait till she's closing."
changes.after: Silas looked away, towards the town. "With half of Kelmend in there? Some bastard would fetch a guard for the price of his next drink. We'll wait till she's closing."
changes.why: Alaric has just said "Tell her Gerolt sent *us*". Silas looking away gives his silence about Marta's rule a visible reason, which the door explains later.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: A hand, not an arm
changes.before: Silas stopped Alaric with an arm across his chest.
changes.after: Silas put a hand up, and Alaric stopped.
changes.why: Silas stopped Alaric with his forearm three times. The one at the tub is kept, because it stops him moving.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: The sack
changes.before: He crouched behind the barrels. Silas pushed the wall door shut and joined him.
changes.after: He crouched behind the barrels. Silas pushed the wall door shut, joined him and took the sack back over his shoulder.
changes.why: Fewer handovers: the sack goes back to Silas in the same sentence, and the separate paragraph goes.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: The sack (2)
changes.before:
"The cart entrance if it's clear," he murmured. "Through the shed if it isn't."

Alaric gave him the sack, and Silas drew its carrying cord over his shoulder.
changes.after: "The cart entrance if it's clear," he murmured. "Through the shed if it isn't."
changes.why: Goes with the change above.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: The far door
changes.before: Silas pointed along the passage inside the shed. Alaric got Wena up without speaking and followed him between the barrels. At the far door, Silas looked through a crack beside the frame, waited, then lifted the latch.
changes.after: Silas pointed along the passage inside the shed. Alaric got Wena up without speaking and followed him between the barrels. At the far door, Silas listened, then lifted the latch.
changes.why: Another look through a gap; listening is enough.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: His brother's daughter
changes.before:
"The guards said his niece." Alaric looked towards the inn. "They meant Marta?"

"Yes. His brother's daughter."
changes.after:
"The guards said his niece," Alaric said.

"His brother's daughter."
changes.why: *His niece.* has already landed, so he doesn't need to ask. Silas's answer adds what's new. 100/100 review: The next line has him looking down at the sword.
changes.decision_note: The review notes (1 October): agreed by the author ("yes apply all").

changes.title: Marta doesn't repeat the ban
changes.before: "Get the fuck out of Kelmend, Silas. Right now." She straightened, her hand falling away from Wena. "I told you I never wanted to see your face again. Did you think I didn't mean it?"
changes.after: "Get the fuck out of Kelmend, Silas. Right now." She straightened, her hand falling away from Wena. "Did you think I didn't mean it?"
changes.why: Silas told Alaric about the ban a minute earlier. Without the repeat, her question points straight back at it.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Her hand on the chain
changes.before: The auctioneer lowered the chain into the man's open hand. The buyer counted the coins into the auctioneer's palm, and the woman had to get down from the platform while they talked. She sat on its edge to do it. The chain tightened before she had both feet on the ground.
changes.after: The auctioneer lowered the chain into the man's open hand. The buyer counted the coins into the auctioneer's palm, and the woman had to get down from the platform while they talked. She sat on its edge to do it. The chain tightened before she had both feet on the ground. She reached up and closed her hand round it, just under her chin. When he pulled again, it pulled her hand.
changes.why: One deliberate act of her own, aimed at the buyer, not at Alaric. The loose chain as she follows now reads as her choice too.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (1)
changes.before: Alaric looked down at Wena. His hand was still gripping the loose skin at her neck; he let it go and stroked her instead.
changes.after: His hand was still gripping the loose skin at Wena's neck. He let it go and stroked her instead.
changes.why: "Looked" was the chapter's most repeated verb (26). Where the look did nothing, it goes.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (2)
changes.before: Alaric looked towards the gate. "Couldn't we just knock at the back? Tell her Gerolt sent us?"
changes.after: "Couldn't we just knock at the back?" Alaric asked. "Tell her Gerolt sent us?"
changes.why: Leaves Silas's "looked away" on its own.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (3)
changes.before: The houses along the wall were closer than they had looked from the slope. They were low and crowded, roof against roof, with the first row built right up against the stones and the next row facing it across a narrow lane. Smoke came out of holes in the roofs as often as out of chimneys. Lamplight showed at the edges of shutters that didn't fit.
changes.after: The houses along the wall were closer than they had seemed from the slope. They were low and crowded, roof against roof, with the first row built right up against the stones and the next row facing it across a narrow lane. Smoke came out of holes in the roofs as often as out of chimneys. Lamplight showed at the edges of shutters that didn't fit.
changes.why: Fewer looks.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (4)
changes.before: Alaric looked at the door. He could hear footsteps and wheels, and somebody telling somebody else they had brought the wrong cart.
changes.after: Beyond the door he could hear footsteps and wheels, and somebody telling somebody else they had brought the wrong cart.
changes.why: Fewer looks.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (7)
changes.before: *A boy and a big dog. That's all they've got.* Alaric looked down at Wena. *And it's enough.*
changes.after: *A boy and a big dog. That's all they've got.* Wena had her head on her paws beside his boot. *And it's enough.*
changes.why: An image in place of a look.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (8)
changes.before: Alaric looked at the strip of cloth in his hand.
changes.after: Alaric's hand closed on the strip of cloth.
changes.why: It shows he doesn't want to let go.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (9)
changes.before: Ahead, a driver was backing another cart into the gap beside the half-unloaded one. People had to step round its shafts. Alaric waited behind the baskets, then looked back to make sure Silas could still see him.
changes.after: Ahead, a driver was backing another cart into the gap beside the half-unloaded one. People had to step round its shafts. Alaric waited behind the baskets, then glanced back to make sure Silas could still see him.
changes.why: Fewer looks.
changes.decision_note: Claude's 100/100 review (1 October), agreed by the author ("the rest apply").

changes.title: Looks (10)
changes.before: Two guards were coming up from the gate with a lantern. Silas looked towards them and shortened Wena's lead again. She saw Alaric turn and tried to come to him.
changes.after: Two guards were coming up from the gate with a lantern. Silas shortened Wena's lead again. She saw Alaric turn and tried to come to him.
